visualReview.notes: Inspected the source preview, four-sided turntable and four details. Three west doors sit beneath the triangular gable and between the open-framed bell crowns. Side and rear views show the glass-lit central lantern, folded nave roofs, narrow wall lights and polygonal sanctuary.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected nine shared-surface frames and confirmed unload. White stone, dark roof seams, glass and timber read distinctly. Roof and bell crown finish retain enough contrast against the marble in the street view.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 current frames across the four detail levels. The skyline frame retains the three towers and cruciform massing; street and closeup resolve open bell frames, portal glazing and the faceted crossing and sanctuary.

geographicReview.notes: The surveyed polygon retains the entrance to the west and polygonal sanctuary to the east. Reviewed the original independent 256 m terrain image and the terrain-mounted street view. The DEM supports the entry mass and foundation; threshold and nearby pavement elevations are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Standing Saint Sarkis Cathedral in Tehran, including its marble-clad single nave, projecting side wings and polygonal apse, its central lantern and conical roof, and two western bell towers.
fidelityReview.notes: The dated University of Tehran architectural survey and Iran tourism inventory support the modeled marble exterior, three west gates, wing and roof forms and glass changes. Heights, roof finish, door joinery and small details of the open bell crowns are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Reviewed Qualla first. Its two public-domain-labeled items lacked reliable provenance for this model and are absent from controls. Used the measured written survey, government description and exact named mapped footprint for the exterior. No photographic reference was used.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The named mapped footprint establishes the surviving exterior. The University of Tehran study and tourism authority document the white marble, polygonal apse, central roof and twin bell towers. Heights, surface details and opening spans are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing Saint Sarkis Cathedral at Karim Khan Street in Tehran, including the west entrances and bell crowns, nave, crossing lantern, side wings and eastern sanctuary.

limitations: The model represents the standing marble-clad cathedral after the west and central glazing changes. The bell tower and dome heights, window spacing and joinery are working estimates.
The source survey records the surveyed form in writing. Exterior visual estimates include the western trim, steel-and-glass bell crowns, marble joints and main roof pitch.

The coarse source ground remains original. Site grade, stair depth and foundation registration are approximate. The detached courtyard monument, precinct wall and Prelacy offices are outside the scope.
